title: Early shuttle crews borrowed yellow U-2/SR-71 suits from Beale
summary: Greg Rogers tells of Early shuttle crews borrowed yellow U-2/SR-71 suits from Beale, about c. 1981 (STS-1 to STS-4) at Beale Air Force Base / Kennedy Space Center, and relays what a named person told them. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Beale Air Force Base / Kennedy Space Center

tellings.quote: they had to go to Beal Air Force Base and borrow the yellow space suits that the U2 and SR71 guys fly.

plain: Greg Rogers, a doctor who worked with NASA, says on Jesse Michels's podcast that the first space shuttle crews, around 1981, including astronauts Young and Crippen, did not have their own pressure suits. According to him, they had to go to Beale Air Force Base and borrow the yellow suits worn by pilots of the U-2 and SR-71, two high-altitude spy planes. He tells it as a glimpse of how closely the space programme leaned on secret military aviation.
